newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep. Archer upbeat tax bill will be signed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep. Archer upbeat tax bill will be signed.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman William Archer, a Texas Republican, said in a statement he was upbeat that congressional negotiators would work out a final tax bill President Clinton could sign.

Archer said he did not agree with proposals in a new $85 billion tax cutting plan unveiled by Clinton Monday that would give low-income families more tax relief. "Putting some differences aside, the president deserves credit and praise for joining with Republicans in endorsing our approach to tax relief," Archer said. "I'm upbeat that we will successfully conference our bills so the president can sign them into law."

Clinton Monday unveiled a new five-year tax plan which contains many of the same elements of legislation already passed by the House and Senate but differs in key respects. One area of disagreement has to do with a $500 per child tax credit. The White House wants the credit partly refundable to ensure lower-income working familes get some benefits.

Archer's version of the bill does not make the credit refundable. In his statement, the tax-writing chairman argued it did not make sense to provide a new tax break to families that pay no income taxes and are already eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit.

"Middle-income workers with high tax burdens aren't eligible for any income support programs, while families that pay no income taxes will receive EITC checks worth up to $3,760 in 1998," Archer said.
He said he looked forward to sitting down with his Senate counterparts to work out a final, compromise bill adding, "I welcome the participation of the White House in this process."
